annotation.title_clean: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee: Health and safety at work – current and future challenges in light of traditional and new technologies, with a focus on AI
annotation.title_en: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee: Health and safety at work – current and future challenges in light of traditional and new technologies, with a focus on AI
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union (C series)
annotation.summary_en: EESC exploratory opinion, requested by the Polish Council Presidency, on occupational health and safety challenges from AI and digitalisation. It recommends worker training, human control over algorithms, worker consultation, social dialogue, a ban on intrusive surveillance, and third-party conformity assessment for high-risk AI. Robotics is mentioned as a source of over-reliance and as a way to reduce risk.
key_provisions_or_claims: Framework Directive 89/391/EEC is the gold standard, but its application needs strengthening.
Calls for human control over algorithms and information and consultation rights on AI in work management.
Recommends banning intrusive electronic surveillance of workers.
Recommends mandatory third-party conformity assessment for high-risk AI systems.
Warns of over-reliance on robotics and loss of worker control without clear roles and training.
